item.title: California Election Special
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Today is voting day across the US and with San Francisco being a very politically charged city, I thought I’d outline some of the major races and ballot initiatives because there’s a lot. As you may know, Arnold Schwarzenegger was allowed to run for governor because they got enough signatures to get it on the [...]
item.content:encoded:
Today is voting day across the US and with San Francisco being a very politically charged city, I thought I’d outline some of the major races and ballot initiatives because there’s a lot.  As you may know, Arnold Schwarzenegger was allowed to run for governor because they got enough signatures to get it on the ballot to boot their governor at the time before his term was up, so the propositions can carry a lot of weight.  I also picked up a handy Voter Guide from the San Francisco League of Pissed Off Voters that I have attached.  It’s kind of frustrating it just tells you what to do, but hey, everybody’s got an agenda.

Makes a good centerpiece

Governor – Jerry Brown (D) VS Meg Whitman (R)

Meg Whitman is the former CEO of eBay and an uber rich, power hungry capitalist, which likely speaks to who she would appease to if voted in, let alone being a Republican.  She has already run the most expensive self-funded gubernatorial campaign in history using an estimated $163 million of her own $1.3 billion personal fortune.  She was on the board of Goldman Sachs and has admitted to making millions spinning IPOs she had access to before the public.  She admitted she didn’t vote at all for a 28 year period.  She thinks illegal immigrants shouldn’t be allowed to attend California schools, yet her housekeeper was one.  She wants to suspend California’s environmental legislation and doesn’t support gay marriage.

Luckily Jerry Brown is ahead in the polls.  He was California governor in the late 70’s and early 80’s, and his father was governor for most of the 60’s.  I have no idea why American’s love a dynasty so much, but at least he’s a Democrat and not Meg Whitman.  He came second in the 1992 Democratic presidential primary to Bill Clinton, has been the mayor of Oakland and is the current California Attorney General where he launched a lawsuit in 2008 against Countrywide Financial for unfair lending practices in the mortgage meltdown.  He has supported green energy his entire career.

Prop 19 – Legalization of Marijuana

Much ballyhooed, I originally was going to try and capture some of the reaction to this race on my blog, then Arnie beat me to the punch by decriminalizing it.  The idea is that pot becomes legal and regulated so the state can make tax revenue on it, which is especially needed by the massively in debt California which has the lowest credit rating of any state.  It’s also obviously a stoner’s dream and supported widely by the youth population.  Seniors and 40 something Generation Xers with teenage kids oppose it.

The summary version

Naturally though, there are always strange hidden machinations behind the scenes.  A lot of local growers I encountered in Humboldt county oppose it because of the commercialization threat to mom and pop operations.  People like Richard Lee, creator of the Oaksterdam University for medicinal growing in Oakland are heavy backers of the bill because they have the ability to instantly mobilize large scale commercial manufacturing and profit immensely.  Phillip Morris wouldn’t be far behind.

And there’s also the gigantic mess it would create immediately following passage.  Could anyone walk into a medicinal dispensary?  Would they sell doobies at 7-11?  The DEA says they would still enforce federal statutes within California.  There was once buzz of federal funding being withheld from the State, and while that has subsided, there is obvious tension.  But for my two cents, that seems like a good thing as one of the major benefits is media attention and possibly spreading the idea to other states.  People I spoke with in Washington and Oregon both said they decided to hold off until 2012 to push for the initiative because more young people vote in presidential election years.  I still hope Prop 19 passes, but something tells me it won’t.

Prop 23 – Suspend California’s Anti-Global Warming Legislation

This one is freaking brilliant.  California voted in 2006 to somewhat follow Kyoto and greatly curb their CO2 emissions, amongst other measures.  One campaign ad will show people laying solar panels or building windmills and fuel cells and say it’s a job creator, another will talk about cap-and-trade and taxation and say it’s a job destroyer.  So it somehow wound up on the ballot to suspend California’s 2006 environmental bill until the State’s unemployment rate is cut in half!  Great wording, they may as well say forever!  Problem is, regulation of emissions and green energy incentives cost money, which California doesn’t have.  But the Texas oil companies backing the bill have plenty!

The long hand

Prop 25 – Allow the State Budget to be Passed with a Simple Majority

In California’s State Legislature, a two thirds majority is required for the budget to pass, or to raise taxes.  Since the Democrats don’t like cutting services and the Republicans don’t like raising taxes, it has lead to a stalemate each of the last several years, sometimes reaching the point where the government had to pay its employees and distribute tax returns in the form of IOU’s.  All this bill is trying to do is get the budget itself back to a 50% + 1 situation so they can actually pass it and not have to spend as much time every year bickering over it.  At the same time, it would potentially allow increases in certain fees and charges (not quite taxes) but I mean hey California, you’re massively in debt, you either have to raise taxes, cut services or go further into debt, it’s your call, but naturally people want none of those three.

Prop L – Illegalize Loitering and Sitting on the Sidewalk in San Francisco

They have both state and local props, and this local one’s good for a laugh: make it illegal to sit on the sidewalk.  San Fran’s a nice town, it stays warm enough, there’s enough hippie vibe going on, so naturally there’s a fair few homeless people.  They don’t have places to sleep, so they go for the sidewalk.  At the same time, San Francisco is an incredibly rich city, so someone in the upper crust decided they didn’t like seeing this while they went to get their latte, and figured they’d use the sledgehammer approach to what is a wide sweeping societal issue.  Newsflash, you’re trying to make being homeless illegal and it won’t work!  I can’t imagine this passing, and the backlash has been fantastic.

item.title: East Hastings
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Before visiting Vancouver’s downtown eastside for the first time, I’d heard more than a few tales about it. Most involved scenes of zombie-like junkies aimlessly wandering with needles stuck in their arms, spilling pills everywhere. It wasn’t quite as ugly as the imagination could paint, but it was definitely pretty bad…in fact, the worst I’ve [...]
item.content:encoded:
Before visiting Vancouver’s downtown eastside for the first time, I’d heard more than a few tales about it.  Most involved scenes of zombie-like junkies aimlessly wandering with needles stuck in their arms, spilling pills everywhere.  It wasn’t quite as ugly as the imagination could paint, but it was definitely pretty bad…in fact, the worst I’ve ever seen.

Wikipedia's take on East Hastings

East Hastings must be the heroin use capitol of North America.  On a Saturday afternoon, the entire block before Main was littered with hundreds of society’s down and outs, some with blankets laid down to display the toaster, hammer and tube socks they’d stolen to sell for dope money, some turning tricks, others putting the torch flame to the crack pipe in plain sight having already scored their 10 bucks by God knows what means.  It’s quite the eye opener, and don’t take this as a recommended ‘must see’, but as long as it’s during the day and you don’t go it alone, it’s really not that dangerous just passing through.

My take on East Hastings

Just passing through and not taking pictures that is.  The number of nasty glares and snarls I got just for having a camera, even if I wasn’t using it was a lot higher than my naivety expected.  Sure, nobody likes to be made a spectacle of, and the natural assumption that I’m somehow exploiting people’s misery is fair from their perspective.  But I’m not, I’m just an observer and I wanted to highlight to people who weren’t there that some serious shit is happening.  I can give you one open license picture from Wikipedia that captures the sentiment, one I took on the corner of Hastings and Main where the guy in the middle clearly looks displeased (a haunting bag lady not in the shot was chirping at me as I clicked with the camera held at my waist to make it not look like it was on), then one of Carnegie Hall where all the dealing goes down.

Shwag, crack, smack, pick your poison

Standing amidst all of this is nothing short of surreal and so I ask my friend acting as a tour guide (not to be confused with the junkie who invited himself to walk with us for five blocks) how can they tolerate so much dealing out in the open.  He replies “oh probably three of the people on these stairs are plainclothes cops, they only care about stopping violence.”  Surveying the scene, I notice one, then two guys standing on the edges of the scrum with radios and a noticeably clean-shaven look.  Dammit, where’s the third?!?!  Dammit, I need to find a better spot to play urban Where’s Waldo!

Cannabis Culture & The New Amsterdam Cafe

In hindsight, the whole afternoon started so innocently at the New Amsterdam Cafe, the stoner’s version of a safe injection site.  For those of you who haven’t been to Vancouver, it’s a cafe where you can sit down, roll a joint and smoke it in broad daylight and nobody cares, just like the real Amsterdam.  They have a marvellous selection of paraphernalia and even make a half decent Americano.

Actually, all of Vancouver is really a stoner’s safe injection site, except for the no smoking in parks bylaw they just passed.  But I mean really, apparently drugs are illegal, yet I went to two spots where everyone in the city knows you can do soft or hard narcotics to your heart’s content.  Or start your own grow up after a visit to the bright neon signed SEEDS store.  I even saw a cash for vial hand to hand 5 feet from a cop.  For those who have seen the 3rd season of The Wire, welcome to Hamsterdam.

This is definitely art

Why do we bother marginalizing the fringes of society so we have reason to judge and imprison them that is haphazardly applied only when it suits us and does nothing to solve the underlying problems?  Would spending the war on drugs money to actually help people be an admission of defeat?  I think Vancouver’s heading the right direction; people aren’t going to start doing heroin because it’s legal, marijuana is less harmful than alcohol or tobacco.  We’ll see how that vote plays out when I get to California.

Maaaaan, I dunno, that’s all I got, it ain’t debate time right now, you know where I stand, maybe just draw your own conclusions and check out my gallery of the New Amsterdam Cafe, East Hastings and Chinatown.

I wouldn’t [...]
item.content:encoded:
“Oh man, you gotta try DMT!”

Nice weather around these parts

This is the start of terrible or excellent advice, no in betweens.  I actually began the conversation by asking “what’s that drug that makes everything turn into a slinky made out of cubes?” having read about it years ago on a site everyone should know about www.erowid.org.  I wouldn’t have known that eating 4 heaping tablespoons of nutmeg gets you sort of woozy and makes you dumb as a brick for two days unless I’d tried it myself…

“DMT!  I haven’t had my mind blown like that in years!”  This is already leading me to believe we’re in the terrible advice category.  Having promised myself at the trip’s outset “no heavy psychedelics”, I’m pretty much already booked to have pupils the size of dinner plates on mushrooms a week from now.  It’s half-terrifying, but equally exhilarating, we can save most of that for another post, I’ll just dabble here.  See my problem with mushrooms is you can’t turn them off, everything just gets more and more intense until your brain explodes and you realize time and space don’t exist; it takes a couple days to put the pieces back together.  When you aren’t a functional member of society though, not a big deal.

Set the controls for the heart of the sun

Even Wikipedia goes so far as to describe DMT as “the businessman’s trip” because it only lasts 15 minutes and the user is still in control and lucid, which is how it was also described to me from first-hand experiences.  It also states “Near-death and mystical states were relatively rare”.  It was even first synthesized by a Canadian!  Now I have to try it, as harmless as basketball and penicillin!

So yeah, just a heads up there’ll be a follow-up on whether the rumours are true sometime in the not too distant future.

item.title: Nelson: Radical Self-Expressionists or Undesirables?
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: It might sound like a strange thing to say, but Nelson feels like a town at war. For those of you not from Western Canada, tucked between the steep slopes and the lake of the Kootenay valley in the Rockies, over 5 hours from Calgary or Vancouver, the 10,000 person town of Nelson is known [...]
item.content:encoded:
It might sound like a strange thing to say, but Nelson feels like a town at war.  For those of you not from Western Canada, tucked between the steep slopes and the lake of the Kootenay valley in the Rockies, over 5 hours from Calgary or Vancouver, the 10,000 person town of Nelson is known as the pot capital of Canada.  25% of all weed smuggled to the US originates from this area.  And so as you might imagine, it has a reputation for attracting a certain type of people.  Like those who quit their jobs, live in a van and like smoking joints.

As long as you're comfortable...

Within 5 minutes of rolling into my first camp spot behind the Safeway, I saw a van technicolour graffitied more than I would have done up Bessie given the chance, and out of it pouring a lot of smoke and a lot of dreadlocks.  This was stereotypical enough to be expected, as I suppose in a way was the fellow I found passed out next to my van at 2:30 AM.  Or perhaps the free yerba mate being given out at one of the vegan cafes the next morning, or the guy practicing long sword in the middle of a soccer field on my way to the beach that afternoon, or the girl who’d shaved part of her eyebrows and slapped some sort of leopard tattoo up there, or…

None of this is really a problem…well, the last one, what’s your opening line “so you like cats?”…but I did come across one guy who kicked his soccer ball past me on the sidewalk so I would briefly join him, we passed it back and forth, I watched him go on ahead and play the same game with a random lady, this time absent-mindedly kicking it into an intersection full of traffic, her barely stopping herself.  Death by lackadaisical hippie?

They must serve food that's EXTREME...ly uncooked. D'oh.

Suddenly the fact dogs, skateboards, hand drums and hacky sacks all are or were banned from downtown at some point doesn’t seem nearly as crotchety.  At the same time, it’s still a free country.  But, for all the pot smoking 20-somethings that like to shred, or disillusioned urban liberals, there’s still a whole whack of lifers, regular old people who own fruit stands and have watched their town change drastically and curse under their breath as they walk down main street wondering why every second restaurant is Thai.  I was wandering down a dusty road I obviously didn’t belong on, a truck pulled over to spray me with dirt and gravel and drove off.  I might not look like I belong, but trust me buddy, compared to most people here I’m just a normal guy.

Obviously too quaint and nice and by the lake to even consider parking here

On the other side of the coin, after a night in the mall parking lot (bylaw officer told me to move along after 4 nights at Safeway) I was having my morning coffee and a guy pulled up in his pickup, asked where I was from, then started going off on how it was bullshit they were trying to rustle me along.  Not seeing the NO OVERNIGHT PARKING! bulletin under my wipers yet, I continued to gradually clue is as he told me the place didn’t used to be like this and there weren’t so many damn cops and everybody was free to do as they pleased.  Amen.

It’s still a great place with a lovely beach and main street, I just found because of the geography and culture I was getting claustrophobic, so I left.

Still, kinda hard to complain about
